purpose: Offer a playful non-circular eye option using a soft diagonally tilted almond with rounded tips.

arguments.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: transparent cartoon game sprite, eye-shape variation v7
Input images: Image 1 is the high-resolution edit target and is absolute authority for the shark body, pose, scale, framing, gray shading, black outlines, waves, yellow mermaid hair, and transparent canvas. Image 2 is the enlarged nearest-neighbor pixel source and Image 3 is the exact original sprite; Images 2 and 3 are authority only for the playful non-circular eye character.
Primary request: Change ONLY the shark's single visible eye in Image 1. Draw one broadly open, playful eye shaped as a soft diagonally tilted almond with rounded tips, echoing the skew and attitude of the original pixel eye. Give it a round black pupil looking forward/right toward the yellow hair. It must feel friendly, eager, and playfully excited, never threatening.
Composition/framing: preserve Image 1 pixel-for-pixel in overall placement and silhouette; retain exactly one visible eye at the same facial location.
Style/medium: polished 2D cartoon sprite with the exact existing palette, line weight, highlights, and shading.
Constraints: preserve the shark body, dorsal fin, snout, water, splash shapes, yellow hair, transparent background, canvas dimensions, pose, and crop. The white eye shape must be clearly non-circular and moderately wide open. Keep the gray skin above/left of the eye completely clean. No eyebrow or brow crease. No mouth or second facial mark. No second eye. No text or watermark.
Avoid: perfect circle, circular eyeball, narrow slit, hostile glare, devious expression, dangerous expression, sharp angular eye, eyelid squint, upper stray dark oval, extra facial marks, changing any non-eye pixels conceptually.
